text:
maya: Heads-up — I sketched a Grafana board idea correlating rack inlet pressure (PDU airflow) + PCIe bandwidth to debug random GPU stalls. Wanted feedback before I wire it up.

arjun: interesting, does inlet pressure come from BMC sensors or separate PDUs?

maya: PDU pressure sensors via the node-exporter plugin — metric is `node_env_inlet_pa`. We also have per-GPU PCIe bytes exported now.

maya: Draft panel set I propose:
- inlet pressure timeseries (per-rack)
- per-GPU PCIe tx/rx rate heatmap
- GPU temp/util timeseries
- scatter: inlet_pa vs pcie_bandwidth (point size = gpu_util)

linh: +1 on the scatter. That should surface cases where inlet dip -> thermal throttle -> PCIe utilization collapse.

sam: do we actually have PCIe per-GPU metrics in prod? I only remember nvlink stats.

maya: yes — ops team merged the exporter change last week. sample PromQL for pcie tx rate:

```
rate(gpu_pcie_tx_bytes_total{device="gpu0",rack="rack-7"}[1m])
```

maya: and inlet pressure example:

```
avg_over_time(node_env_inlet_pa{rack="rack-7"}[5m])
```

arjun: alert idea: when inlet_pa < 950 Pa AND avg_gpu_temp > 75°C AND pcie_bandwidth drops > 40% over baseline for 3m -> page (P2). Put longer debounce for P1s. We need to reduce noise during CRAC cycles.

maya: agreed. We'll annotate CRAC cycles using `crac_unit_state` metric so we can mute alerts during expected cycles.

ops-bot: deploy log: grafana/provisioning/dashboards/ -> added draft `inlet-pcie-combo.json` to staging at 1959991300 by maya

linh: will you add an alternative panel that shows rack-level aggregates? sometimes per-gpu is too noisy.

maya: yes — rack-aggregate heatmap + top-5 offending GPUs table. Also add a scatter regression line to highlight correlation.

sam: quick cost note — high-res (1s) scrapes for PCIe across whole fleet will blow remote_write. Can we scope high-res to 10% of racks (sampling) and keep 15s otherwise?

maya: plan: relabeling job `gpu_high_res` targets only `high_res_racks.txt`. I'll open PR with relabel_config snippet.

arjun: also add a per-dashboard toggle to switch between `high-res` and `default` queries (via template var). makes debugging easier without changing global scrape config.

maya: will do. I'll include example templated queries in the dashboard JSON. Example templated query for scatter:

```
scatter_series(
  avg_over_time(node_env_inlet_pa{rack="$rack"}[${window}]),
  rate(gpu_pcie_tx_bytes_total{rack="$rack"}[${window}])
)
```

linh: for alerts, let's target a 3-stage policy: warn (slack) -> escalation (pager) -> auto-mitigation hint (ops playbook link).
sam: I'll run an estimate of added remote_write bytes for 10% high-res by EOD.

arjun: next steps: maya PR for dashboard + templated queries, linh to draft alert rules + playbook snippets, sam cost delta. ETA: EOD Friday?

maya: EOD Friday works. I'll ping here with PR + snapshot.

linh: awesome — this fills a gap for those weird PCIe/fan interactions.
sam: :thumbsup:
